cross.title: Primordial black holes production in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
cross.summary: We consider models with the Gauss-Bonnet term multiplied to a function of the scalar field and propose a new inflationary model which provides a mechanism for the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). For certain values of the model parameters, the predictions of this model agree with observational data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). Due to estimation of possiable PBHs masses, we demonstrate that they can be considered as a possible source for all or part of dark matter.

cross.title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
cross.summary: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only $\sim$$10^{-4}$ of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion $S \lesssim B$, where those are the signal and background counts. We advocate that xenon detectors instead utilize most of their dark-electron rate (i.e., the total raw electron hit rate) and perform an annual-modulation search, for which the sensitivity scales as $S \lesssim \sqrt{B}$. Modern DAQs already record this rate, continuously in triggerless systems such as the XENONnT and PandaX-4T DAQs, and within trigger windows in LZ, so no new hardware is required. Using measured dark-electron rates, we estimate the sensitivity of XENONnT, LZ, PandaX-4T, PandaX-xT, and XLZD. We find that dramatic gains in sensitivity are possible, motivating new analyses of present and future xenon data.

cross.title: Higgs-portal dark matter beyond kinetic equilibrium
cross.summary: We revisit the scalar, vector, and fermion Higgs-portal dark matter models in the resonant regime without assuming kinetic equilibrium during the freeze-out. We compute the relic abundance by solving the full momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation and compare the results with the standard momentum-averaged treatment. We find that the standard treatment significantly underestimates the relic abundance below the resonance, apart from the fermionic case with a purely scalar portal coupling where the difference is negligible. The deviation from the standard treatment is largest for fermionic models with pseudoscalar interactions, corresponding to factor of 10 in terms of the coupling that reproduces the correct relic abundance. For the scalar and vector cases the corresponding difference is up to a factor of 2. We confront the resulting parameter space with the latest constraints from direct and indirect detection, as well as collider experiments. We find the full momentum-dependent results systematically strengthen the direct detection constraints.

cross.title: Kinetic moment estimates and a one-sided Lyapunov barrier for the relativistic fermionic Michie-King equation
cross.summary: We study the cutoff Ruffini--Argüelles--Rueda (RAR), or relativistic fermionic Michie--King, equation of state along an equilibrium family with fixed Tolman--Klein invariants. Three kinetic moments give exact formulas for both the pressure-to-density ratio and the derivative of pressure. Cauchy--Schwarz yields a global relation between these two quantities. It implies vertical vector-field domination of the associated Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff system by the linear equation of state $P=\rho c^2/\sqrt3$ in the physical wedge $0<y\leq3x$. We construct a filled, one-sided version of the Bors--Stańczy Lyapunov barrier and check every boundary. This controls all outward excursions, including those after a lower exit from a Lyapunov sublevel. For regular configurations the resulting explicit Lambert bound is $2Gm(r)/(rc^2)<0.6879212521$. Using the diagonal where this ratio has a stationary value sharpens the bound to $0.6734385929$. The argument is conditional on a regular TOV configuration and does not require a separate finite-radius existence theorem. We also identify and correct a logarithmic coefficient in the previously used explicit linear-comparator formula.

cross.title: Finite-Temperature Stabilization of a KKLT Modulus in Three-Dimensional Lattice Simulations
cross.summary: We investigate the cosmological stabilization of a KKLT modulus through three-dimensional Langevin lattice simulations incorporating an evolving thermal bath, dissipation, spatial gradients, and stochastic fluctuations. While the spatially averaged modulus closely follows homogeneous evolution away from the capture threshold, near-critical trajectories linger near the unstable potential barrier for approximately one e-fold, allowing long-wavelength fluctuations to undergo tachyonic amplification and drive localized regions across the barrier even as the mean field turns back toward the stabilized vacuum. Linear Langevin theory reproduces the fluctuation growth, while convergence tests identify a narrow stochastic layer in which the barrier-crossing fraction shows no systematic dependence on the discretization at a fixed effective distance from the threshold. These results demonstrate that capture of the spatially averaged modulus does not guarantee that every spatial region remains within the stabilizing barrier.

cross.title: Quantifying the Impact of Galactic Dark Matter Halo Models on LZ Results
cross.summary: Most dark matter direct-detection limits are reported under the assumption of an isotropic, Maxwellian Standard Halo Model. However, the Milky Way's stellar halo exhibits substantial radial anisotropy, while cosmological simulations predict scale-dependent anisotropy in the dark matter velocity distribution. We investigate how departures from isotropy affect the interpretation of LZ results in two complementary regimes: background-dominated elastic-scattering searches and the recently reported 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate, which we study using a background-free single-event approximation. For elastic scattering, we use the self-consistent isotropic, Osipkov-Merritt, axisymmetric, and triaxial halo models of Belli et al. and translate the published limits through the ratio of predicted event counts, applying a common escape-speed truncation in the Galactic frame. At WIMP masses above approximately 40 GeV, the resulting limits lie within about $\pm 30\%$ of the isotropic reference. Below approximately 15 GeV, the model envelope broadens to as much as an order of magnitude, reflecting sensitivity to the high-velocity tail. For the 248 keV event, the accessible inelastic mass splitting is likewise controlled by this tail. Some anisotropic models extend the allowed kinematic region towards splittings at which solar-neutrino constraints on a Higgsino interpretation become ineffective, although kinematic accessibility alone does not establish viability at the fixed Higgsino cross section. These results show that halo-model dependence is modest at high WIMP masses but becomes essential near kinematic thresholds.

cross.title: A novel mechanism for coherent radio emission: particle-in-cell simulations
cross.summary: It has been established that electron (phase-space) holes, i.e., EHs, can arise from the nonlinear relaxation of the electron beam instability. Excitation of electromagnetic waves related to the EHs is, however, still not fully understood. Using 2.5-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations, we systematically investigate the nonlinear evolution of the (moderately relativistic) electron bi-stream instability (a special case of the electron beam instability where the densities of the two counter-propagating energetic electron beams are equivalent) in charge- and current-neutralized plasmas under weak and strong magnetizations. This study provides new insights into the wave excitation, the nonlinear wave-particle interactions, the formation of non-Maxwellian features, and the anisotropic electron heating in magnetized plasmas, with potential implications for coherent radio emission in astrophysical plasmas (e.g., solar zebra-pattern bursts).

cross.title: Radial Evolution of Correlation Anisotropy in PUNCH Observations of the Young Solar Wind
cross.summary: Solar wind turbulence, evolving in the presence of a mean magnetic field, large-scale shear, and expansion, exhibits several types of anisotropy, including wavevector anisotropy and variance anisotropy. As the solar wind expands from the corona into the interplanetary space, the magnetically controlled outer corona transitions into the dynamic and less constrained solar wind, and fluctuations may evolve toward isotropy. This is suggestive of an evolution of anisotropy with distance from the Sun, a feature observed in earlier results using surveys of in-situ data, as well as more limited images of solar wind density from STEREO. Here we confirm and expand on those results employing data from the PUNCH mission, whose wide-field, high-cadence imaging enables anisotropy tracking at different heliospheric positions. We evaluate a two-dimensional (2D) correlation function $C(\ell_{\perp}, \ell_{\parallel})$ of polarized white-light brightness as a function of radial $\ell_\parallel$ and transverse $\ell_\perp$ scales to infer the nature of density anisotropy and its development in space. At larger heliocentric distances ($\sim 100 R_\odot$), circular contours of the correlation function indicate a transition toward approximate isotropy. The correlation structure at heliocentric distances from $30R_\odot$ to $60R_\odot$ preferentially extends along the radial direction, which might imply the possible dominance of the two-dimensional variation in the transverse plane. In this way, the very large field of view of PUNCH images reveal a fundamental transition of solar wind turbulence toward isotropy.

cross.title: Gravitational waves in hierarchical triples with lensing and relativistic orbits
cross.summary: Binary black holes (BBH) may be formed near galactic nuclei. If such BBH systems exist, modulations to the gravitational waveform through time delays, lensing, and angular momentum precession could allow the presence of the third body to be measured in this system. In this letter, we advance the modeling for hierarchical triples by carefully including new relativistic lensing, aberration, and polarization terms. We show that the gravitational waves from this system can be computed exactly in the geometric optics limit by ray tracing the null geodesics and parallel transporting their polarization without a weak-field expansion. Our construction evolves the inner binary as if it were a post-Newtonian signal, and computes the environmental modulations efficiently with elliptic integrals. We find that this method improves the accuracy of such a triple waveform significantly compared to previous post-Newtonian approximations, and allows numerically efficient computation of the modulations. This lays the groundwork for future hierarchical triple waveform codebases, which can be used in LISA parameter estimation and detectability.

cross.title: Pseudoscalar Yukawa Preheating via Effective Action Approach
cross.summary: In this work, we investigate helicity-dependent fermion production driven by a pseudoscalar Yukawa interaction within the one-loop effective action framework. By integrating out the fermionic fields and employing the Schwinger proper time representation, we derive an analytical expression for the fermion pair production probability near each zero crossing of the oscillating inflaton field. We further introduce a helicity transfer matrix to describe the evolution of fermionic modes through successive non-adiabatic production events. For an undamped inflaton background, the temporal symmetry around successive zero crossings leads to the cancellation of helicity-mixing contributions after an even number of events, preventing the accumulation of helicity asymmetry. We then extend the analysis to a damped oscillatory background, in which the decreasing inflaton amplitude breaks this temporal symmetry and modifies the transfer matrix at each crossing. The resulting non-commuting transfer matrices produce a persistent helical spectrum, as demonstrated by the probabilities as a function of momentum obtained after successive scattering events. A comparison with scalar Yukawa preheating further confirms the role of helicity mixing in generating the helical asymmetry induced by pseudoscalar mechanism. These results establish an effective action framework for studying helicity asymmetry during fermionic preheating and provide insight into the influence of the inflaton's dynamical evolution on particle production.

cross.title: Revisiting RadioGalaxyNET: modern detectors for radio galaxy detection and host identification
cross.summary: RadioGalaxyNET is the public benchmark for finding extended radio galaxies in EMU pilot-survey images, classifying them and locating their infrared hosts. Its best published results date from 2023: 54.5 box AP (Gal-YOLOv8) and 48.1 host keypoint AP (Gal-DINO). We train three current detectors, D-FINE-seg, YOLO26-pose and RF-DETR, on the same data and score them with the benchmark's own evaluation code, which reproduces the published Gal-DINO numbers exactly. All exceed the published results. D-FINE-seg M reaches 67.1 box AP and 72.4 host AP, 12.6 and 24.3 points above the best published results, and the highest host AP of the detectors we tested; on boxes it is level with YOLO26. Its host lead over YOLO26 comes from host-centered images, which make up most of the benchmark. End to end, D-FINE-seg S is the fastest model at 1.9 ms per image; engine against engine, YOLO26 is faster at the same size. We also report what matters for anyone using the benchmark: its scoring protocol adds 5 to 10 AP, its host labels sit at the image center, its box labels are offset from the image by 1.5 pixels, and its images can be rebuilt from the public survey data, which recovers sky positions and doubles as extra training data. We suggest that future work report host identification F1, as a measure closer to catalog use: D-FINE-seg M 71.8, YOLO26-pose M 70.5, RF-DETR 63.8, Gal-DINO 59.2.

cross.title: World Models Are the Right Foundation for Simulating Mars Terraforming
cross.summary: Terraforming Mars is a long-horizon, action-conditioned control problem that requires predicting atmospheric responses to interventions over centuries to identify effective policies. This position paper argues that physics-regularized recurrent state-space world models are the most promising foundation for this setting. Data-driven climate emulators lack action-conditioning, and physics-based general circulation models (GCMs) are too expensive for policy search. Among learned world models, recurrent state-space architectures with physics constraints are better suited than transformer-based alternatives: they provide native uncertainty quantification through their stochastic-deterministic decomposition, remain stable under sparse non-terrestrial training data, and enforce physical consistency at each rollout step. To make this position concrete, we describe a potential architecture combining JEPA-inspired latent encoding, universal differential equation constraints, and a Dreamer-lineage planning head. We also introduce MarsWorld, an open benchmark proposal for intervention-conditioned planetary world models, and discuss broader implications and objections.

cross.title: Superheavy gravitational dark matter from runaway bubble collisions
cross.summary: A stable particle that couples only through gravity is pair-produced in collisions of runaway bubble walls by graviton exchange. For a transition of duration $1/\beta$, a Dirac fermion reaches the yield $Y_X\simeq6.8\times10^{-3}(H/\beta)(T_{\rm reh}/M_{\rm P})^3$, where $H$ is the Hubble rate of the vacuum energy, $T_{\rm reh}$ the reheating temperature and $M_{\rm P}$ the reduced Planck mass. The yield is flat up to masses near $(H/\beta)M_{\rm P}/\nu^2$, where $\nu$ of order one sets the wall-field excursion. Gravity alone then gives dark matter up to about $10^{17}$~GeV at reheating temperatures far below its mass, where freeze-in fails.

cross.title: Post-Newtonian expansion of the energy and angular momentum flux radiated to infinity: Eccentric-equatorial orbits about a Kerr black hole
cross.summary: We present analytical expressions for the energy and angular momentum fluxes radiated to infinity by a (nonspinning) point mass in an eccentric-equatorial orbit about a Kerr black hole. These results build upon our previous work involving point masses on eccentric orbits about a Schwarzschild black hole. We now adopt the Teukolsky formalism in first-order black hole perturbation theory to extend our methods to Kerr. We obtain the expressions using the method of Mano, Suzuki, and Takasugi, which provides infinite-series analytical solutions to the Teukolsky equation that we generate using Mathematica. The expressions presented are obtained as a double expansion in the post-Newtonian (PN) compactness parameter $1/p$, where $p$ is the dimensionless semi-latus rectum, and in the eccentricity $e$, up to 10PN and $e^{20}$, extending beyond prior 6PN and $e^{16}$ results available for generic orbits. We characterize how the PN flux coefficients depend on the black hole spin $a$ and $e$, and find a set of spin-dependent components that can be resummed as closed-form expressions in $e$. The analytical expressions are then validated with numerical comparisons against high-precision sample results from an independent Teukolsky code and with a broader set of numerically interpolated values derived from a flux data set produced with the same code. For $a=0.9M$, the numerically evaluated 10PN fluxes match current interpolated flux grids ($\sim10^{-7}$) for $p\gtrsim20$ to $75$ as $e$ ranges from $0.1$ to $0.7$, where they could replace Teukolsky-code results.

cross.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
cross.summary: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass $1.4+1.4M_\odot$ binary with both stars at a redshifted temperature $T_\infty=10^5\,\mathrm K$ and a standard electron shear viscosity, tidal dissipation shifts the gravitational-wave phase by less than $10^{-3}$ cycles between $20\,{\rm Hz}$ and $1\,{\rm kHz}$ for the four equations of state considered. Including the resulting rise in the stars' temperature in a simple thermal model reduces the shift below $10^{-6}$ cycles. For the viscosity model considered here, shear-viscous tidal dissipation in cold neutron stars is negligible for gravitational-wave phasing. This suggests that a measurable dissipative tidal signature would have to come from a different mechanism.

cross.title: The Science Chapter of the Einstein Telescope Geometry Comparison Report
cross.summary: This is the Scientific Added Value Chapter of the Einstein Telescope (ET) Geometry Comparison Report, commissioned from the ET Organization by the ET Board of Governmental Representatives. We compare three configurations: a single-site 10-km triangle ($\Delta$) and two 15-km L-shaped detectors (2L) at widely separated sites, either nearly aligned or misaligned. We use metrics representative of the ET science case: compact-binary populations, dense matter, cosmography, stochastic backgrounds, multimessenger astronomy, fundamental physics, and continuous and burst sources. All three configurations deliver the ET science case, but they excel in different areas. For most sensitivity-driven science, the 2L configurations outperform the $\Delta$. The misaligned 2L is best for localizing and characterizing individual sources, multimessenger astronomy, and bright-siren cosmology. The nearly aligned 2L is best for stochastic backgrounds. The $\Delta$ localizes sources better than the aligned 2L and performs comparably to both 2L configurations for continuous and burst sources and at kilohertz frequencies. A 2L orientation of $30^\circ$ is a good compromise between stochastic-background sensitivity and localization. We validate Fisher information matrix (FIM) forecasts against Bayesian inference for $\sim550$ binary black hole and neutron star-black hole signals. Despite substantial differences, the FIM shows no systematic preference for either configuration for intrinsic parameters. For distance and sky localization, the FIM cannot capture multimodality and long-range correlations, leading to larger discrepancies, which however do not affect the ranking. Adding Cosmic Explorer to the network improves the reach of all three ET configurations, especially in volume localization and characterization of high-redshift sources. Differences between geometries shrink, but the ranking is largely unchanged.

cross.title: Exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon field in planar systems with an arbitrary number of uniform layers
cross.summary: Scalar fields have long been investigated as a potential dark energy candidate. Of these models, screened scalar fields like the chameleon have received interest due to their ability to avoid observational constraints. However, the non-linear nature of these models has led to there being only a small number of exact analytic solutions within the literature. In this work, we present exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon model in a planar system consisting of $N$ discrete regions of uniform density. We compare these to the relevant approximate solutions within the literature. We also use our solutions to forecast constraints from CANNEX, a recent experiment devised to measure Casimir forces and detect hypothetical fifth forces. Unlike in previous works, we consider the full fifteen-layered setup of CANNEX, as opposed to treating the plate and wall as single uniform objects. Doing so revealed an increase in the induced chameleon pressure of up to $\sim 7 \%$. However, the resulting gain is insufficient to probe new regions of parameter space at the projected sensitivities.

cross.title: Analytic $k$-essence Inflation
cross.summary: In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dot{\phi}^2=\gamma H^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters $n$ and $m$. The resulting evolution is inflationary and it develops a pressure singularity a few $e$-foldings after the end of inflation. However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.

cross.title: Relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for Kerr black holes
cross.summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) observed by LISA will probe the environments of massive black holes (BHs), including the dark matter (DM) overdensities expected to form around them. We compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a Kerr BH embedded in a collisionless DM distribution, extending previous results in Schwarzschild. The DM is modeled as a spike grown adiabatically from an initial Hernquist profile, and the momentum transfer is obtained by integrating relativistic scattering and capture cross sections over the full, generically anisotropic phase space seen by the secondary. Far from the primary the friction tracks the local DM density, which increases with spin. Near the innermost stable circular orbit of rapidly spinning BHs $(a\gtrsim 0.37)$, however, frame dragging forces bound DM particles to co-rotate, so that the secondary is overtaken by the surrounding medium: the friction weakens and eventually reverses sign where the DM density peaks. We show that a similar reversal can be mimicked around a non-rotating BH if the initial halo carries large net angular momentum, although this requires anisotropies beyond those found in cosmological simulations. We also show that commonly used Chandrasekhar-like prescriptions, which depend only on the local density, can overestimate the friction force. Our results demonstrate that the full phase-space structure of the environment must be included when modeling DM effects on EMRIs.

cross.title: Enhancing eccentricity through tidal resonance in binary neutron star systems
cross.summary: Orbital eccentricity of binary neutron star systems is a key parameter to reveal their formation history. Since binaries formed in isolation are expected to circularize long before merger, measurable eccentricity suggests dynamical formation in dense stellar environments. However, using numerical-relativity simulations, we show that eccentricity can be introduced in the late inspiral of an initially quasicircular binary, due to the $f$-mode resonance of one of the stars. We simulate the merger of two highly spinning neutron stars, one star spinning prograde and the other retrograde. Persistent tidal resonance with the $f$ mode of the retrograde-spinning star is observed, accompanied by a gradual change of its spin due to angular momentum transfer from the orbit. This spin change can be well explained by a simple resonance locking model that accounts for the spin-dependent shift of the $f$-mode frequency. These findings reveal an origin of eccentricity in binary neutron stars that is independent of their formation history and provide important information for modeling binary neutron star dynamics with rapidly spinning stars.

cross.title: Optimal Statistic for a Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background using Pulsar-Timing--Astrometry Cross Correlations
cross.summary: Astrometric measurements have emerged as a viable probe of gravitational waves (GWs), complementing pulsar timing searches by providing overlapping and higher GW frequency coverage. At its core, the search for GWs using astrometry is very similar to the search with pulsar timing data: GWs induce a change in pulse arrival times along the line of sight to a pulsar and a transverse angular deflection in the apparent position of a star. In analogy to pulsar timing, we develop a correlation statistic between pairs of stellar deflections for astrometry to search for a stochastic GW background. With a common formalism for both astrometry and pulsar timing, we also develop the cross-correlation statistic between stellar deflections and pulsar timing residuals. We estimate the signal-to-noise ratios from the correlation statistics and provide scaling laws in the weak- and intermediate-signal regimes.

repl.title: Primordial B-mode sensitivity forecasts for northern-sky cosmic microwave background surveys
repl.summary: Northern-sky cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarization observations offer additional sky coverage and independent measurements in the search for primordial gravitational waves. We assess their potential through idealized sensitivity forecasts motivated by the Ali CMB Polarization Telescope. Using a power-spectrum likelihood and Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling, we relate assumed map depths, accessible angular scales, and effective sky coverage to constraints on the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. The model retains lensing B modes and assumes negligible residual foreground power. A benchmark with 95 and 150\,GHz channels, a polarization map depth of $40\,\mu\mathrm{K\,arcmin}$ per channel, and $f_{\rm sky}=0.1$ yields $\sigma(r)=0.023$ for a fiducial $r=0.014$, improving to 0.015 with Planck-like mock data. At a per-channel depth of $10\,\mu\mathrm{K\,arcmin}$, the northern survey alone reaches $\sigma(r)=0.0031$. Raising the minimum multipole from 30 to 70 degrades the baseline sensitivity to 0.037, while extending the effective area at fixed depth improves the constraint. As the northern maps deepen, their contribution increasingly determines the precision on $r$, whereas Planck-like information continues to constrain the scalar spectral index. These forecasts quantify the scope for improved northern-sky tensor constraints and establish sensitivity benchmarks for subsequent studies of joint northern and southern CMB observations.

repl.title: Quantum cosmological perturbations in bouncing models with mimetic dark matter
repl.summary: We calculate the power spectrum of cosmological perturbations originated from quantum vacuum fluctuations in bouncing scenarios proposed in Ref.~\cite{chamseddine2014cosmology} in the framework of mimetic cosmology. We show that all physically relevant models produce scale-invariant spectral indices and amplitudes compatible with observations, provided that the bounce occurs at length scales $t_0$ inside the physically reasonable interval $10^5 l_p < t_0 < 10^9 l_p$. We also show that by slightly modifying the scalar field potential proposed in Ref.~\cite{chamseddine2014cosmology}, we can obtain the observed red-tilted spectral index, with the same amplitude constraints. The underlying theory contains instability problems yet to be solved. However, the methods we constructed and the results we obtained may be sufficiently general to be applied to the infrared limit of some yet to be constructed healthy mimetic cosmology, providing reasonable bouncing cosmological models without the need for any background quantum effect.

repl.title: CMB constraints on $U(1)$ axion warm inflation
repl.summary: In this work, we propose a model of warm inflation driven by axion-like particles interacting with $U(1)$ gauge fields, with implications for the early universe's thermal evolution. By extending traditional warm inflation models, we introduce a dissipation mechanism through the thermal fluctuations of electromagnetic fields, leading to a non-trivial back-reaction on the inflaton's dynamics. Our results are consistent with CMB observations, even for a natural sub-Plankian Axion decay constant $f\leq M_{\rm Pl}$. We present precise constraints on the model's free parameters, using CAMB and CosmoMC codes. These findings offer new insights into the thermal history of the universe and the nature of inflationary dynamics.

repl.title: Rapid late-time reionization: constraints and cosmological implications
repl.summary: We present constraints on the reionization optical depth, $\tau$, obtained using several independent methods. First, we perform a non-parametric reconstruction of the reionization history, using Lyman-$\alpha$ constraints on the evolution of the volume-averaged neutral hydrogen fraction, $x_\mathrm{HI}(z)$, including recent results from JWST. When combined with BAO measurements from DESI and BBN constraints, these data imply a rapid reionization history ($z_\mathrm{mid}=6.99^{+0.12}_{-0.18}$ and $\Delta z_{50}=1.09^{+0.10}_{-0.28}$) and a value of $\tau=0.0491^{+0.0014}_{-0.0031}$, which is largely insensitive to the assumed cosmological model and independent of CMB data. The optical depth can also be measured from large-scale $(\ell<30)$ CMB polarization data, yielding constraints that are similarly model-insensitive and consistent with the Ly$\alpha$ bound. Third, $\tau$ may be constrained from the attenuation of small-scale $(\ell>30)$ CMB anisotropies, but the results are sensitive to the choice of cosmological model. Assuming $\Lambda$CDM and combining small-scale CMB data with CMB lensing and type 1a supernovae (SNe) yields tight constraints that are compatible with the Ly$\alpha$ bound. Adding galaxy clustering and lensing measurements brings the constraints further into agreement with the Ly$\alpha$ bound. These independent results reinforce a consensus picture in which reionization is rapid and late. However, the combination of small-scale CMB, CMB lensing, and BAO data yields $\tau=0.094\pm0.011$, which is in $4\sigma$ tension with our Ly$\alpha$ bound. Non-standard reionization scenarios, or relaxing our assumption that the onset of reionization occurs after $z=15$, can reconcile some but not all constraints. Concordance is restored in alternative cosmological models, such as models with dynamical dark energy favoured by BAO, CMB, and SNe data.

repl.title: How Bright in Gravitational Waves are Millisecond Pulsars for the Galactic Center GeV Gamma-Ray Excess? A Systematic Study and Implications for Dark Matter
repl.summary: The existence of dark matter (DM) is supported by various macroscopic observations, but its microscopic nature remains elusive. The Galactic Center GeV gamma-ray excess (GCE) has been a leading candidate signal for particle DM annihilation. However, an unresolved population of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in the bulge provides the alternative explanation for the excess. Identifying these MSPs in electromagnetic bands is difficult due to source confusion, pulse broadening, and extinction. Gravitational waves (GWs) provide a complementary probe: a steadily rotating, non-axisymmetric MSP emits a nearly monochromatic GW signal in the sensitive band of ground-based detectors, with amplitude set by its ellipticity. In this work, we systematically investigate the GW emission from the MSP population proposed to explain the GCE and its detectability with current and future detectors. We consider three major scenarios for the origin of ellipticity and model the population properties of these MSPs. We also consider both isolated MSPs and MSPs in binary systems, as well as Doppler effects in the detection. We find that while the signal is below the reach of current interferometers, next-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) may detect a fraction of those MSPs, offering a novel test of the MSP interpretation of the GCE. Future directed searches toward the Galactic Center may either uncover this long-sought MSP population or place stringent constraints on bulge MSP properties. Continued improvements in detector sensitivity will provide increasingly stringent tests of the MSP interpretation, with growing power to distinguish between the astrophysical and DM interpretations of the GCE.

repl.title: Solving the Domain Wall Problem: Primordial Magnetic Fields as a Dynamical Solution
repl.summary: To prevent overclosing the Universe, stable domain walls must decay-a problem typically addressed by breaking the Peccei-Quinn symmetry with a bias term. In this Letter, we present a novel mechanism in which a helical primordial magnetic field provides a spatially inhomogeneous Chern-Simons source that drives the axion field. We validate this mechanism through three-dimensional lattice simulations of the evolving domain-wall network, demonstrating its efficacy in inducing decay. Our quantitative analysis reveals that the correlation length of the primordial magnetic field is a crucial determinant of the decay rate of the network and the properties of the emitted axions and gravitational waves. In particular, the axion emitted from the decaying domain-wall network can contribute to the dark matter abundance, and the associated gravitational-wave signal lies in the frequency range probed by pulsar timing array experiments.

repl.title: Analysis of LIGO glitches during the first part of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run
repl.summary: This paper presents an analysis of noise transients observed in LIGO data during the first part of the fourth observing run, using the unsupervised machine learning technique t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) to examine the behavior of glitch groups. Based on the t-SNE output, we apply Agglomerative Clustering in combination with the Silhouette Score to determine the optimal number of groups. We then track these groups over time and investigate correlations between their occurrence and environmental or instrumental conditions. At the Livingston observatory, the most common glitches during O4a were seasonal and associated with ground motion, whereas at Hanford, the most prevalent glitches were related to instrumental conditions.

repl.title: Wavelet-domain flow-matching posterior estimation for LISA signals with data gaps
repl.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) data stream will contain scheduled and unscheduled gaps, which break the stationarity of the instrumental noise and invalidate the standard frequency-domain likelihood. Amortized simulation-based inference (SBI) avoids explicit likelihood evaluations, but its application to months-long observations requires compressing high-dimensional, gapped time series while preserving information about source parameters. We develop an end-to-end amortized posterior estimation pipeline: the gapped data are mapped to noise-scaled Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer (WDM) wavelet coefficients and summarized by a convolutional-Transformer network, trained jointly with a flow-matching (FM) posterior estimator, with optional importance-sampling correction. For a LISA-like signal observed for 3 months, the amortized FM posteriors are well calibrated on simulated observations whose waveforms and gaps were not seen in training. The FM posteriors agree closely with the benchmark, the posteriors from parallel-tempered Markov chain Monte Carlo (PTMCMC), although they exhibit moderately greater dispersion. Importance sampling efficiently reweights the FM posterior, achieving close agreement with the benchmark at modest additional cost.

repl.title: Observational constraints on early time non-phantom behaviour of dynamical dark energy
repl.summary: We investigate dynamical dark energy models in which the scalar field component is non-phantom at early times. The models include a single-exponential thawing field, a double-exponential scaling--thawing field, and extensions in which a steep exponential scaling field is combined with a cosmological constant, a constant-$w$ fluid, or a CPL fluid. We confront them with Planck PR4 CMB temperature, polarisation and lensing data, DESI DR2 BAO measurements and the Pantheon$+$ supernova sample. The background parameters are stable across all models, with $H_0 \simeq 67.7$--$68.3\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, so none of the models relieves the Hubble tension. The CPL parametrization prefers $w_0>-1$ and $w_a<0$ at $\sim\!2.7\sigma$ relative to $\Lambda$CDM, corresponding to phantom behaviour at low redshift. The constant-$w$ and thawing models remain consistent with a cosmological constant. When an early scaling phase is added, the data limit the peak early dark energy fraction to $f_{\mathrm{EDE}}<0.0075$ ($f_{\mathrm{EDE}}<0.015$ for SC$+$CPL). This requires a steep potential, $\lambda_2 \gtrsim 30$, and keeps the scalar-field density below the half-percent level at matter--radiation equality. Early scaling dynamics therefore cannot alter the sound horizon enough to address the Hubble tension. The scaling models fit the data as well as $\Lambda$CDM ($\Delta\chi^2_{\mathrm{min}}\lesssim 1.4$), but they are disfavoured by AIC and BIC because of their additional, weakly constrained parameters. Adding a scaling field to CPL does not improve the fit. Late-time evolving dark energy is mildly preferred by the data, while a simple early scaling phase offers no benefit.

repl.title: A single field inflationary model consistent with recent observations: reheating and radiative stability
repl.summary: We study single field inflation with the inverse exponential potential, which has one free parameter besides the energy scale. For a wide range of parameter space, its predictions for the scalar spectral index and the tensor to scalar ratio lie within the $1\sigma$ region of the combined SPA$+$BK$+$DESI data, and the wider family of inverse power law exponential potentials behaves similarly. We compare these predictions with those of the $R^2$ model, monomial potentials, $\alpha$-attractors, non-minimally coupled Higgs like inflation and a radiatively corrected plateau potential. The $R^2$ and monomial predictions lie near or outside the $2\sigma$ boundary of the same data, whereas the non-minimally coupled Higgs like and radiatively corrected plateau families overlap the favoured contours over part of their parameter space. To describe reheating, we add a steep exponential term that is negligible during inflation and, together with the inverse exponential term, creates a minimum about which the inflaton oscillates. The maximum reheating temperatures are $T_{\rm rh}\sim10^{12}$--$10^{13}\,{\rm GeV}$, consistent with the Big Bang Nucleosynthesis bound. Coupling the inflaton to a Dirac fermion through a Yukawa interaction, these temperatures require couplings comparable to the standard model charged lepton Yukawa couplings. Nonperturbative fermion production transfers negligible energy, and perturbative decay completes reheating. The same coupling induces a one loop correction to the inflationary potential, which limits the radiatively safe reheating temperature to $T_{\rm rh}\lesssim10^{12}\,{\rm GeV}$.

repl.title: The Impact of Galaxy Formation on Galaxy Biasing, and Implications for Primordial non-Gaussianity Constraints
repl.summary: The parameter $f_{\textrm{NL}}$ measures the local non-Gaussianity in the primordial energy fluctuations of the Universe, with any deviation from $f_{\textrm{NL}}=0$ providing key constraints on inflationary models. Galaxy clustering is sensitive to $f_{\textrm{NL}}$ at large scale modes and the next generation of galaxy surveys will approach a statistical error of $\sigma_{f_{\textrm{NL}}}\sim1$. However, the systematic errors on these constraints are dominated by the degeneracy of $f_{\textrm{NL}}$ with the galaxy bias parameters $b_1$ (galaxy overdensities caused by mass perturbations) and $b_{\phi}$ (galaxy overdensities caused by primordial potential perturbations). It has been shown that the assumed scaling of $b_{\phi}(z)=2\delta_c (b_1(z)-1)$ is not accurate for realistically simulated galaxies, and depends both on the galaxy selection and the way that galaxies are modeled. To address this, we leverage the CAMELS-SAM pipeline to explore how varying parameters of galaxy formation affects $b_{\phi}$ and $b_1$ for various galaxy selections. We run separate-universe N-body simulations of $L=205 h^{-1}$ cMpc and $N=1280^3$ to measure $b_{\phi}$, and run 55 unique instances of the Santa Cruz semi-analytic model with varying parameters of stellar and AGN feedback. We find the behavior and evolution of a SC-SAM model's stellar-, SFR- and sSFR- to halo mass relationships track well with how $b_1$ and $b_{\phi}(b_1)$ change across redshift and selection for the SC-SAM. We find our variations of the SC-SAM encapsulate the $b_{\phi}$ behavior previously measured in IllustrisTNG, the Munich SAM, and this http URL , we identify sSFR selections as particularly robust to varied galaxy modeling.

repl.title: Correlation Calibration: A Hybrid Calibration Technique for Radio Interferometric Arrays
repl.summary: Calibrating out per-antenna signal chain effects is an essential step in analyzing radio interferometric data. For drift-scanning arrays, robustly calibrating the data is especially challenging due to the lack of the ability to track a calibration source. Consequently, calibration strategies for drift-scanning arrays are limited by our knowledge of the radio sky at large, as well as the direction-dependent instrument response. In the context of 21 cm cosmology, where small calibration errors can conspire to overwhelm the cosmological signal, it is therefore crucially important to develop calibration strategies that are capable of accurately calibrating the data in the presence of sky or instrument modeling errors. In this paper we present CorrCal, a covariance-based calibration strategy for radio interferometric arrays. CorrCal is a hybrid calibration strategy that leverages the strengths of traditional sky-based calibration and redundant calibration in a computationally efficient framework that is fairly insensitive to modeling errors. We find that calibration errors from CorrCal are unbiased and far below typical thermal noise thresholds across a wide range of modeling error scenarios. We show that CorrCal is computationally efficient: our implementation is capable of evaluating the likelihood and its gradient in less than a second for 1,000-element class arrays using just a single laptop core. Given CorrCal's computational efficiency and robustness to modeling errors, we anticipate that it will serve as a useful tool in the analysis of radio interferometric data from current and next-generation experiments targeting the cosmological 21 cm signal.

repl.title: Dark Energy Survey Year 6 Results: Cosmological Constraints from Cosmic Shear
repl.summary: We present legacy cosmic shear measurements and cosmological constraints using six years of Dark Energy Survey imaging data. From these data, we study ~140 million galaxies (8.29 galaxies/arcmin$^2$) that are 50% complete at i=24.0 and extend beyond z=1.2. We divide the galaxies into four redshift bins, and obtain cosmic shear measurement with a signal-to-noise of 83, a factor of 2 higher than the Year 3 analysis. We model the uncertainties due to shear and redshift calibrations, and discard measurements on small angular scales to mitigate baryon feedback and other small-scale uncertainties. We consider two fiducial models to account for the intrinsic alignment (IA) of the galaxies. We conduct a blind analysis in the context of the $\Lambda$CDM model and find $S_8 \equiv \sigma_8(\Omega_m/0.3)^{0.5}=0.798^{+0.014}_{-0.015}$ (marginalized mean with 68% CL) when using the non-linear alignment model (NLA) and $S_{8} = 0.783^{+0.019}_{-0.015}$ with the tidal alignment and tidal torque model (TATT), providing 1.8% and 2.5% uncertainty on $S_8$. Compared to constraints from the cosmic microwave background from Planck 2018, ACT DR6 and SPT-3G DR1, we find consistency in the full parameter space at 1.1$\sigma$ (1.7$\sigma$) and in $S_8$ at 2.0$\sigma$ (2.3$\sigma$) for NLA (TATT). The result using the NLA model is preferred according to the Bayesian evidence. We find that the model choice for IA and baryon feedback can impact the value of our $S_8$ constraint up to $1\sigma$. For our fiducial model choices, the resultant uncertainties in $S_8$ are primarily degraded by the removal of scales, as well as the marginalization over the IA parameters. We demonstrate that our result is internally consistent and robust to different choices in calibrating the data, owing to methodological improvements in shear and redshift measurement, laying the foundation for next-generation cosmic shear programs.

repl.title: Pulsar Timing Array in the past decade
repl.summary: The past decade has been a transformative period for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and their search for nanohertz gravitational waves (GWs). This progress has been driven by collective advances in instrumentation for pulsar timing observations, increasingly sophisticated data-analysis techniques, and improved theoretical understanding of the origins of nanohertz GW signals. PTA sensitivity has steadily improved, leading first to progressively more stringent upper limits on the gravitational-wave background (GWB), and subsequently to the identification of a common red-noise process in pulsar timing data, the first hint of a GWB. In 2023, multiple PTA collaborations reported evidence for the Hellings-Downs correlation, widely regarded as the definitive signature of a GWB. These developments place PTAs on the threshold of a confident GW detection and the opening of a new low-frequency window on the GW Universe. In this article, we present an overview of PTA experiments, with particular emphasis on the rapid progress achieved during this pivotal period for PTA and nanohertz GW science.

repl.title: Modeling individual nearby radio galaxies as ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray accelerators
repl.summary: Nearby radio galaxies are among the most promising candidates for the acceleration of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs). In this work, we develop a physically motivated, source-resolved framework to quantify the contribution of the three nearest FR-I radio galaxies$-$Centaurus A, Virgo A, and Fornax A to the UHECR flux measured by the Pierre Auger Observatory. Acceleration spectra derived from detailed jet-acceleration models are combined with numerical simulations of extragalactic propagation, while the more distant radio-galaxy population is treated as a continuous background. By fitting exclusively the measured UHECR energy spectrum, we determine the relative contribution of each source and constrain the fraction of jet power converted into UHECR luminosity. We find that a small number of nearby radio galaxies can account for the highest-energy UHECR flux with acceleration efficiencies of order $10^{-3}-10^{-2}$, while the background contribution remains subdominant. The resulting scenarios yield mass-composition trends broadly consistent with observations and predict distinct levels of secondary neutrino fluxes. These results demonstrate that physically grounded, source-specific modeling of nearby radio galaxies provides a viable and predictive explanation for the origin of the highest-energy cosmic rays.

repl.title: The Marked Power Spectrum as a Practical Bispectrum Measure for Galaxy Redshift Surveys
repl.summary: Modern datasets have the precision necessary to uncover new information by including higher-order, non-Gaussian information into cosmological inference. The marked power spectrum offers access to such information while preserving the structure of two-point correlators. This approach to higher-order statistics has the advantage that many modeling questions can directly benefit from progress already made in standard cosmological analyses using the power spectrum and correlation function, while increasing the data vector size negligibly and retaining much of the degeneracy-breaking power of the bispectrum through a particular data compression. In this work, we first restructure the marked power spectrum to isolate its higher-order information and demonstrate its ability to break parameter degeneracies. We then investigate the effect of survey geometry on the marked power spectrum and find that a treatment similar to that of the power spectrum is sufficient. Additionally, we investigate the perturbative modeling and covariance structure of the marked power spectrum, shedding light on its degeneracy breaking power and cross-covariance with the power spectrum. Finally, we demonstrate that the cosmology dependence of the marked power spectrum is smooth, indicating that cosmological inference is possible by modeling the cosmology dependence through interpolation rather than analytical modeling.

repl.title: An OASIS of Lyman-$α$ within a neutral intergalactic desert: reaffirmed line and blue continuum reveal efficient ionising agents at $z = 13$
repl.summary: $\require{mediawiki-texvc}$Galaxy assembly was already well underway in the first 400 Myr of cosmic time, as revealed by JWST. However, the contribution of these early galaxies to cosmic reionisation remains uncertain. Here we present new JWST/NIRSpec observations of GS-z13-1-LA from the OASIS and JADES programmes, whose combined deep (56 h) NIRSpec/PRISM spectrum confirms the previously reported Lyman-$\mathrm{\alpha}$ line detection and blue UV continuum at redshift $z = 13.1$. The measured Lyman-$\mathrm{\alpha}$ emission (rest-frame equivalent width of $66_{-9}^{+10}\,Å$) and steep continuum slope ($\beta_\text{UV} \approx -3$) point towards GS-z13-1-LA hosting a remarkably hot and powerful ionising source, and allow at most a modest contribution from the nebular continuum. The steep turnover of the continuum is markedly less pronounced in the new OASIS spectrum, suggesting a lower HI column density covering the source (or OASIS sightline). Combined, this implies that ionising photons may escape GS-z13-1-LA fast enough to weaken the other, still undetected UV lines, and lead to the formation of a small ionised bubble ($R_\text{ion} \approx 0.2\,\mathrm{pMpc}$, depending on model assumptions). A yet larger bubble could alleviate the required ionising photon production efficiency of GS-z13-1-LA from $\xi_\text{ion} \approx 10^{26.4}\,\mathrm{Hz\,erg^{-1}}$ down to $\approx 10^{25.9}\,\mathrm{Hz\,erg^{-1}}$, still extreme but more reconcilable with stellar models. In turn, this would require a notable overdensity of galaxies with highly efficient ionising capabilities, for which we find tentative evidence in 17 nearby photometric candidates and one spectroscopically confirmed source, JADES-GS-z13-0. The new OASIS observations thus confirm the overall picture of GS-z13-1-LA as an early beacon of reionisation, providing compelling evidence for its start only 330 Myr after the Big Bang.

repl.title: An intertwined short and long $γ$-ray burst with a 4-minute separation
repl.summary: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), among the most energetic transients in the Universe, are traditionally classified into long-duration (lasting more than 2 seconds) and short-duration (lasting less than 2 seconds) events. Long-duration GRBs are typically associated with the core collapse of massive stars (type II), whereas short-duration GRBs originate from the merger of compact binary systems (type I). These different progenitor channels are reflected in distinct observational signatures that provide key diagnostics for GRB classification. Here we report a peculiar event, GRB 160425A, comprising two sub-bursts separated by 4 minutes: a short-duration burst ($G_1$) and a long-duration burst ($G_2$). Nearly all standard prompt-emission diagnostics, including pulse morphology, duration, hardness ratio, minimum variability timescale, spectral properties and established empirical correlations, consistently categorize $G_1$ as a short-like GRB (type I, merger origin) and $G_2$ as a long-like (type II, collapsar origin) GRB. The coexistence of merger and collapsar signatures within a single event challenges existing progenitor frameworks and calls for a re-evaluation of GRB classification schemes and progenitor scenarios.

repl.title: Visual Characteristics of a Rotating Black Hole in $4$D Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity with Thin Accretion Disk Under EHT Constraints
repl.summary: This study investigates the visual characteristics of a rotating black hole (BH) within the fabric of $4$D Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity illuminated with two illumination models, such as a celestial light sphere and a thin accretion disk. To visualize the BH shadow images, we use a recent fisheye camera model and ray-tracing method. And then, we focus on investigating the impact of the coupling parameter $\alpha$ and the spin parameter $a$ on the shadow images. The results exhibit that the shadow radius decreases, while the shadow deviation increases with the aid of $\alpha$. However, with respect to $a$, the shadow radius is slightly increased compared to the corresponding shadow deviation. For a celestial light sphere, the increasing values of $\alpha$, lead to a decrease in the corresponding photon ring, while the space-dragging effect becomes more prominent with increasing $a$. For a thin accretion disk, we enhance its inner edge to the BH event horizon, and the particle motion is different in the regions inside and outside the innermost stable circular orbit. The result demonstrates that the shadow becomes progressively asymmetric with $a$, while the overall size of the inner shadow gradually decreases with the variations of $\alpha$. Subsequently, we also investigated the distinct features of red-shift configurations on the disk for both direct and lensed images. Additionally, we used the latest observational data from M87* and Sgr A* to impose certain parameter constraints on $\alpha$; the results depict the consistency of our considering the BH model.

repl.title: Advance warning of $γ$-ray blazar flares from Fermi-LAT light curves: a strictly causal machine-learning backtest
repl.summary: Long-term Fermi-LAT monitoring makes it possible to ask whether a blazar light curve shows signs of an upcoming flare before it becomes obvious in the $\gamma$-ray emission. We present a strictly causal machine-learning framework for forecasting $\gamma$-ray blazar flares from 3-d binned LAT light curves. Flare intervals are identified with Bayesian Blocks, and 42 variability features are measured from 365-d trailing windows. We train separate WATCH and TRIGGER models: WATCH predicts whether flare activity will appear within the next 90 d, while TRIGGER predicts whether a new flare onset will occur within the next 45 d. To avoid temporal leakage, all scaling, calibration, threshold selection, and validation use only pre-cutoff data (before MJD 60000). We apply the method to the FSRQ 4FGL J1048.4+7143, using 13 bright blazars as auxiliary training sources. Among logistic regression, polynomial logistic regression, and random forest classifiers, polynomial logistic regression gives the strongest held-out WATCH performance, with ROC AUC = 0.884, average precision = 0.392, and a block-permutation probability $p_{\rm perm}$ = 0.009. At the selected threshold it recovers 21 of the 21 positive WATCH windows. For TRIGGER, the same model gives AUC = 0.751, but with just nine positive test windows its AP = 0.121 is only about twice the random baseline (0.052), and no reliable pre-onset TRIGGER alert is obtained. The WATCH state appears before both held-out flares, with alerts 4.5 and 2.5 d before onset. These results suggest that the Fermi-LAT light curve of this source contains useful predictive information about its flare build-up during the period considered.

repl.title: Mitigating residual foregrounds and systematic errors in SKA1-Low AA* EoR observations via Bayesian Gaussian Process Regression
repl.summary: The redshifted 21-cm line is an emerging tool in observational cosmology that can serve as a direct probe of the intergalactic medium throughout the cosmic timeline. However, the observation of the cosmological 21-cm signal is extremely challenging in practice, regardless of the scale of interest and redshift, due to the presence of astrophysical foregrounds and residual systematic errors. Machine-learning-based Gaussian process regression (ML-GPR) has proven to be the most effective strategy for signal separation in LOFAR and NenuFAR observations to measure the 21-cm signal power spectrum from the Cosmic Dawn (CD) and Epoch of Reionization (EoR). In this work, we extend this framework to synthetic CD/EoR SKA1-Low observations to assess its robustness in mitigating residual foregrounds against instrumental and environmental systematic effects. We use our developed end-to-end realistic simulation pipeline (21cmE2E) for SKA-Low observations. Our 4-hour tracking simulation includes extragalactic point sources, the AA* telescope configuration, primary beam response, and residual systematics. The modelled errors incorporate antenna-based gain calibration errors, ionospheric phase errors, partial de-mixing of the out-of-field sources, and instrumental noise for 1000 hours of deep integration time. This work is one of the first demonstrations of the efficacy of the ML-GPR method in a realistic observing scenario. We compare different Bayesian GPR frameworks to assess their ability to suppress residual foreground contamination while minimising signal loss and providing reliable uncertainty estimates. Our results demonstrate that even in a realistic scenario where observations have a combination of residual systematics, ML-GPR can recover the 21-cm signal robustly within the $2\sigma$ confidence interval across almost the entire range of k-modes sampled.

repl.title: Assessing the imprint of eccentricity in GW signatures using two independent waveform models
repl.summary: The gravitational-wave signal from merging compact binaries encodes information about their orbital and intrinsic properties. Over the last few years, state-of-the-art waveform models have begun to incorporate the effects of orbital eccentricity into their estimated signal. Over a similar period, many groups have applied these waveforms to characterize whether the imprint of eccentricity is present and, if so, measure this time-evolving property (at a suitably-defined reference point). In this work, we present a comprehensive analysis of 162 confident sources identified in the O3 and O4a observing runs of the International Gravitational Wave Network (LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA). Using the RIFT parameter inference engine, we employ two independently implemented waveform models (SEOBNRv5EHM and TEOBResumS-Dali) which account for orbital eccentricity and the effects of aligned compact object spins. Using these two waveforms, we find consistent conclusions that disfavor the eccentric hypothesis. Unlike previous work, among binary black hole candidates, we find potential evidence for eccentricity in three events: GW200129, GW231001, and GW231123. For the latter two events, the evidence for eccentricity is ambiguous, with different degrees of support from different waveforms. Consistent with previous work, we find conclusions obtained about GW200129 can be sensitive to analysis settings, as expected, given the nonstationary noise present.

repl.title: Temporal evolution of the periodic GeV signal from 4FGL J1913.2+0512 and analysis of the SS 433/W50 lobes
repl.summary: SS 433 is a microquasar whose relativistic jets precess every ~162 days, providing a laboratory for jet-interstellar medium interactions. We present a comprehensive analysis of 16 years of Fermi Large Area Telescope data (August 2008-September 2024) of the SS 433/W50 field, using events in the 0.3-300 GeV range and employing pulsar gating to mitigate contamination from the bright nearby pulsar PSR J1907+0602. We detect the GeV source 4FGL J1913.2+0512 (TS = 45, where TS denotes the likelihood-ratio Test Statistic) with a power-law spectrum (photon index 2.61 +- 0.08) and confirm a GeV excess at the western lobe (TS = 17). The eastern lobe of SS 433 is hinted at with lower significance. One additional GeV excess, Fermi J1909.6+0552 (TS = 20; TS = 28 over 0.1-300 GeV), located outside the SS 433/W50 system, is revealed after gating. Exposure-corrected Lomb-Scargle periodograms and precessional phase-folded light curves show a ~162-day modulation in 4FGL J1913.2+0512. The phase-folded emission is mainly confined to the first half of the precessional cycle, while the source is not significantly detected in the second half. This periodic signal is mainly concentrated in the 5-10 yr interval, remains visible in the cumulative 0-10 yr data set, and is not recovered in the subsequent 10-16 yr interval. Over the full 16-year data set, the modulation remains detectable but with reduced significance, consistent with dilution by the later non-modulated epoch. These results indicate that the efficiency and/or geometry of gamma-ray production in the SS 433 environment evolves on multi-year timescales.

repl.title: Development and ground demonstration of a Modular Astrobiological Experiments (MAEx) payload for autonomous biological monitoring in Low Earth Orbit (LEO)
repl.summary: The spaceflight environment presents unique challenges for biological systems, including microgravity, ionizing radiation, altered fluid transport, and confined habitats. Understanding and harnessing biological processes under these conditions are essential for future space biomanufacturing, including biological production and bioregenerative life-support technologies. Such applications require compact, autonomous experimental platforms capable of monitoring biological responses to spaceflight stressors. Here, we present the ground-based validation of the Modular Astrobiological Experiments (MAEx) payload, a compact 3U platform designed to support future autonomous biological investigations in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). MAEx integrates three analytical modules: camera-based imaging, optical spectroscopy, and microbial electrochemistry. Its versatility was evaluated using three biological systems: the electroactive bacterium Shewanella oneidensis MR-1, the radiation-resistant fungus Ustilago maydis FB1, and the human eye-lens protein {\gamma}D-crystallin. The imaging module was validated by monitoring microbial growth over time, while the spectroscopy module was evaluated for its ability to detect changes associated with microbial growth and protein aggregation. The electrochemical module was functionally validated by monitoring anodic current production during S. oneidensis MR-1 cultivation. Together, these results demonstrate the functionality of the three analytical modules and establish MAEx as a ground-validated TRL-4 platform. The MAEx architecture provides a foundation for future investigations relevant to space biomanufacturing, bioregenerative life-support, and in situ resource utilization. Environmental qualification for spaceflight remains ongoing, and further development is required before the payload can be integrated into existing or planned orbital laboratories.

repl.title: Metamorphoses of carbon and oxygen in protoplanetary discs: how chemistry and radial drift transform inner disc C/O ratios
repl.summary: The chemical composition of a protoplanetary disc is sensitive to its thermal structure and dust properties, and can provide insights into the disc evolution. Recent observations with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) reveal correlations of the inner disc compositions with disc size, accretion rate and stellar mass, explained by the key role of dust radial drift in redistributing primordial volatiles. We explore how chemical reactions change the composition of ices carried with pebbles and how they affect the inner disc C/O ratios in a disc around a solar mass star. We consider different drift efficiencies set by dust fragmentation velocity and include dust traps at different locations. We vary the incident cosmic ray ionisation rate $\zeta$ and the efficiency of cosmic ray dissociation of ices, and consider the effect of carbon grain destruction. We find that methane depletion within $<1$ Myr prevents the delivery of carbon-rich gas to the inner disc and yields $\mathrm{C/O} \lesssim1$ for $\zeta\geq10^{-17}$ s$^{-1}$. Dust traps collect water and carbon-rich ices formed via methane destruction, further lowering the inner disc metallicity and C/O ratio. Cosmic-ray driven photodissociation of ices can convert water to O$_2$ and carbon-bearing molecules to CO, allowing ices to escape the trap if $\gtrsim10 \%$ of the dissociated products can participate in surface reactions. We discuss the observational implications and conclude that cosmic rays and their effect on ices are the key factors that determine the impact of chemistry on the inner disc composition.

repl.title: Beyond Self-Similarity: Reconciling X-Ray Scaling Relations in Galaxy Clusters and Groups
repl.summary: Scaling relations hold among observed quantities that describe the thermodynamic properties of the gas in galaxy clusters and groups. However, observed data show systematic departures from the self-similar model's baseline predictions, particularly in lower-mass systems. I show that the observed departures from self-similar predictions can be efficiently described by two physical quantities modeled with power laws: the gas mass fraction $f_g$ and the temperature variation $f_T$. Using a wide range of published X-ray scaling relations, this study conducts an MCMC-based meta-analysis to constrain the temperature- and redshift-dependence of the meta-parameters $f_g$ and $f_T$ and calibrate the model. These calibrations indicate that, while the gas mass fraction does not show significant evolution with cosmic time, it decreases significantly with decreasing halo mass. On the other hand, the temperature variation shows a mild positive increase with both mass and redshift. Overall, modeling the departures from the self-similar model with $\{f_g, f_T\}$ drastically improves predictive accuracy, reducing the number of scaling relations in $>3\sigma$ ($>5 \sigma$) tension from 49 (36) percent under the self-similar scenario to just 8 (3) percent (three and one out of 39, respectively) that might be identified for their peculiarity. Moreover, modeling through this generalized framework allows for an extended discussion of the expected slopes and redshift evolution for several X-ray scaling laws, including the new quantity $Y_{LGT0} = L^{-1} M_g^2 T^{a_L}$, a proxy for the cluster's volume that is independent of $f_g$ and $f_T$ by construction, and is predicted to scale directly with mass with a well-defined redshift evolution ($M \sim Y_{LGT0} f_g^0 f_T^0 E_z^2$), as validated against hydrodynamical simulations and observational constraints.

repl.title: Peristaltic Flow in Compressible, Ideal Magnetohydrodynamics: A Mechanism For Solar Spicules
repl.summary: We present an analytical model for peristaltic transport within compressible, ideal magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). By employing a small-amplitude perturbation expansion, under a thin-tube long-wavelength approximation with a uniform axial background magnetic field, we study non-linear coupling between thermodynamic pressure variations and Maxwell's magnetic tension stresses. The resulting net time-averaged conserved mass flux $\langle \dot{M} \rangle$ is calculated. When applied to solar chromospheric spicules under equipartition constraints ($\beta \sim 1$), where sound speed matches the Alfv{é}n speed, we find $\langle \dot{M} \rangle = 8\epsilon^2/(M^2-1)^2$. Because the denominator remains strictly positive across all operational supersonic Mach numbers ($M \approx 2\text{--}10$), upward-propagating mechanical disturbances drive a highly directional, collimated upward flow which we interpret as a spicule. Estimates show that for observationally realistic magnetosonic waves with amplitudes of $\approx 10\%$, the peristaltic mechanism generates a localized mass flux up to $\approx 100$ times that of the solar wind. We show that because high-Mach waves suffer strong compressible choking, small-amplitude perturbations preferentially select low-supersonic modes ($M \approx 1.05\text{--}2.0$) to drive spicule-level mass loading. We propose an explicit observational signature of this mechanism, wherein the launch of individual spicular jets is directly preceded by magnetosonic wave trains detectable as localized intensity modulations. Beyond solar chromospheric application, the model may be applicable to traveling magnetic field pinches in laboratory plasma devices and astrophysical mass-loading processes in stellar winds and inner regions of magnetized accretion disks.

repl.title: Dark Energy Survey Year 3 results: optimized $w$CDM simulation-based inference with weak lensing map-level hybrid statistics
repl.summary: We present cosmological constraints from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3) weak lensing data using hierarchical hybrid statistics within a Bayesian simulation-based inference framework that is based on the Gower Street simulations. To maximize the precision of the inference, we have developed a new, information-theory based, data compression of the weak lensing maps to just seven highly informative summary statistics. The hybrid scheme exploits the high information content of the power spectrum, compressing both the power spectrum and neural-based summaries that are designed to extract further information. Our simulation-based approach enables principled forward modelling of all major sources of systematic uncertainty and survey properties into realistic mock observations, including the survey mask, photometric redshift uncertainties, intrinsic galaxy alignments, multiplicative shear calibration bias, source galaxy clustering, non-Gaussian shape noise, and non-linear structure formation. The summary statistics are then used in a Bayesian simulation-based inference pipeline. The inference is validated through coverage tests and checks for robustness against baryonic feedback. Assuming a $w$CDM cosmology, our analysis yields $S_8 = 0.808 \pm 0.017$, $\Omega_{\rm m} = 0.325 \pm 0.024$, and $w < -0.766$ (marginalized posterior 68 per cent credible intervals). This rigorous combination of information theory, physics- and neural network-based extreme data compression, and principled Bayesian analysis improves the figure of merit for $(\Omega_{\rm m}, S_8, w)$ by 60 per cent over the previous state-of-the-art, and by almost a factor of 3 over two-point analyses of the same data. They are the most precise joint constraints on $(\Omega_{\rm m}, S_8, w)$ from weak gravitational lensing data alone of any survey to date. We intend to apply this analysis to the more recent DES Y6 data.

repl.title: Tracking low-velocity ejecta from the DART impact on Dimorphos
repl.summary: The DART impact on Dimorphos produced a large population of low-velocity ejecta (v < vesc), likely containing most of the excavated mass, whose early fate remains poorly constrained. We investigate the first 22 h evolution of ejecta launched at 1-9 cm/s and assess how orbital dynamics and surface transport after first contact shape the surface distribution of the re-accreted ejecta blanket. We use RAVEL, a model that couples three-dimensional orbital dynamics in the Didymos-Dimorphos system with surface transport on a digital terrain model, including detachment, re-impact, rebound, and frictional sliding. Re-accretion is rapid and asymmetric: more than 99% of the re-accreted mass returns to Dimorphos within 5 h. The slowest ejecta remain concentrated near the DART crater and dominate the primary ejecta blanket, whereas faster particles undergo orbital transport and preferentially populate antipodal and trailing regions. Surface motion strongly modifies the first-contact pattern, and the DART-derived rough terrain model produces elongated, topographically channelled depositional streaks dominated by the slowest ejecta, giving rise to a ray-like pattern. These results provide testable predictions for ESA's Hera mission and link ejecta-blanket morphology to orbital dynamics, re-accretion, and surface topography.

repl.title: Forward-modelling the Tolman and distance-duality tests with IllustrisTNG
repl.summary: The Tolman surface-brightness test and the angular-size distance-duality test are two complementary probes of the same underlying relation between luminosity and angular-diameter distance, $D_L = (1+z)^2 D_A$, as holds in any metric theory of gravity where photon number is conserved. Both tests have recently delivered a priori surprising signals: JWST/ASTRODEEP measurements yield a surface brightness scaling with redshift much flatter than the expected value, and ultracompact radio sources also appear to follow a flatter $D_L/D_A$ scaling with redshift. These results have been suggested to support non-expanding cosmologies, however they are also sensitive to astrophysical and instrumental effects. We test whether these results indicate genuine departures from standard cosmology by forward-modelling observed surface-brightness evolution in the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation, with an empirical mock-spectroscopic selection trained on ASTRODEEP. We show that the astrophysical evolution relevant for both tests may be effectively parametrised as a single power-law exponent for the luminosity density as a function of redshift, for which the simulation gives $\gamma=2.23\pm0.20$ across realistic aperture conventions. This value is approximately sufficient to explain both the Tolman and distance-duality signals within standard cosmology and galaxy formation physics, with a small discrepancy for the latter suggesting that radio AGN evolve slightly more strongly than bright galaxies.

repl.title: Constraining dark energy with complementary probes of large-scale structure
repl.summary: To observationally pin down the nature of dark energy, it is essential to consistently model cosmological perturbations in the presence of dark energy alongside the background expansion and constrain this joint theory space with a large array of complementary probes. Here, we achieve this by constraining a model in the Effective Field Theory of Dark Energy (EFTofDE) framework by supplementing probes of the expansion history with several probes of large-scale structure: redshift space distortions (RSD) from DESI DR1, $3\times2$pt measurements from DES Y3, and the Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect from cross-correlating CMB temperature anisotropies with galaxy number counts or CMB lensing. We demonstrate the complementarity of different probes which leads to strong improvements on constraints on DE perturbations. For our most constraining dataset combination that supplements CMB+BAO+SNe probes with DESI DR1 RSD, DES Y3 $3\times2$pt and ISW cross-correlations between CMB temperature and galaxy counts, we find an improvement in the Figure of Merit (FoM) for the DE perturbation parameters $\{c_B, c_M\}$ by a factor of 2.69. We show the phenomenological implications of these constraints by mapping them to the present-day values of the phenomenological functions $\{\mu(z), \Sigma(z)\}$, where we see an FoM improvement by a factor of 3.37. We find a significant interdependence between the posteriors of $\{w_0, w_a\}$ and $\{c_B, c_M\}$, caused by the theoretical prior imposed by the gradient stability condition within the EFTofDE framework. Finally, we compute the significance of deviation from $\Lambda$CM for the EFTofDE model when constrained with CMB+BAO+SNe datasets, finding it to be at 2.9$\sigma$. This significance is nontrivially similar to the significance for the $w_0w_a$CDM model for the same dataset combination which we find to be 3.1$\sigma$.
